one_liner: Senior Executive who runs the Education Department's small business office, setting goals and policy so small and disadvantaged firms win more ED contracts.
fit_summary: This is an SES position requiring demonstrated executive leadership (all five ECQs) plus hands-on experience leading a small business utilization or federal acquisition program and applying the FAR. Daniel's policy knowledge, relationship skills, and government-contractor consulting experience at IEM are relevant context, but nothing on file shows executive-level leadership or FAR/small business program management. Unless Daniel's IEM role involved substantial federal contracting leadership, the resume is unlikely to pass the ECQ/TQ panel and OPM's Qualifications Review Board.
eligibility: Open to the public (hiring paths include public and SES), so no federal status is needed; U.S. citizenship is required.
The two-page resume itself must show all five ECQs and both TQs; failing to address any one means disqualification, and separate narratives are not accepted.
TQ 1 requires demonstrated experience leading a small business utilization or federal acquisition program, and TQ 2 requires applying the FAR and small business contracting rules.
You must obtain a Public Trust clearance, file an OGE-278 financial disclosure, and receive OPM QRB approval before appointment.
The application window runs from October 23 to November 6, 2026.
strategy: Before investing time, check honestly whether your IEM work included leading people and managing federal contracts, proposals, or subcontracting plans. If it didn't, treat this as a target for later and look at GS-1102 contract specialist or GS-0301 program analyst roles to build FAR experience.

If you do apply, frame IEM as work on federal and state emergency-management contracts. Include any work on small business subcontracting plans, teaming with small firms, FEMA or HUD contract compliance, or proposal pricing, describing only what you actually did.

Write each bullet so it visibly maps to a specific ECQ or TQ, using the posting's language (for example, 'Driving Efficiency' or 'measurable performance goals'). Reviewers stop reading at page 2, so put the strongest ECQ/TQ evidence on page 1.
Use ECQ 1 to show your deep knowledge of the American system of government and public policy, backed by concrete examples of work rather than general interest.
Quantify everything you can: team size you led, budget or contract dollars managed, and percentages of goals met. Use 10-point font or larger, and include dates and hours per week for each job.
Submit well before November 6, 2026, and confirm that the uploaded resume renders at exactly two pages.
resume_bullets: Led a team of [number] on [client] [disaster recovery/preparedness] contracts valued at $[amount], tracking deliverables against [metric] and achieving [result].
Coordinated with [federal/state agency] officials and [number] subcontractors, including [small/disadvantaged] firms, to ensure compliance with [FAR clause/contract requirements] on [project].
Analyzed [legislation/policy] affecting [program] and briefed [senior leaders/clients] on recommended actions, which led to [outcome].
interview_questions: How have you used the FAR to develop an acquisition strategy that increased small business participation?
Describe how you would negotiate annual socioeconomic goals with SBA and with ED's two procurement offices.
Tell us about a time you led a team through change and held people accountable for results.
How would you use data-based metrics to show whether OSDBU is meeting its targets?
watch_outs: SES-level requirements, including executive leadership and direct small business or acquisition program experience, likely exceed your documented background, and OPM QRB approval is an added hurdle.
The two-week application window is short, and any ECQ or TQ left unaddressed means automatic disqualification.
The job is based in DC with telework eligibility, but it is not remote, the position may be detailed to another agency, and relocation is not paid.
